land.text: the Chagatai ulus within the Mongol Empire: 'the regions roughly corresponding to the defunct Qara Khitai Empire' (Issyk-Kul, the Ili, Chu and Talas rivers, Transoxania, the Tarim Basin)

predecessors.note: The ulus dates from 1227 ('When Genghis Khan died in 1227, his son Chagatai Khan inherited ...') and the infobox calls it 'Independent Khanate (1266–1347)'; Cliopatria draws it only from 1294, the first year of the four successor rows, and this dossier follows Cliopatria. The ulus before 1294 is inside the Mongol Empire shape.

land.text: the Moghul khanate after Esen Buqa II's death: 'in the west Yunus Khan gained power, while in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Moghulistan row begins in 1463; 'After the death of Dost Muhammad in 1469, Yunus Khan reunited the khanate' (Moghulistan page).

capitals.name: Almaliq
capitals.note: Moghulistan infobox 'Capital: Almaliq'; the Chagatai infobox lists 'Almaliq, Qarshi' with no years, and Tughlugh Timur is buried at Almaliq. Later seats are undated: Uwais Khan 'eventually made Turfan his main base of residence' and moved 'to Ilibalik in Ili River Valley' under Oirat attacks; Esen Buqa II 'moved to Aksu'. Qarshi (65.8 E, 38.87 N), the seat of the western Chagatayids, is not given years by either page.

keyframe_review.note: 2.46 M km2 against the infobox's 3.4 M km2 ('1310 or 1350 est.'), ratio 0.72. Transoxiana (93%), Fergana, Tashkent, Semirechye, the Tarim (66%) and Almaliq are inside, as the page's 'Issyk-Kul, the Ili, Chu and Talas rivers, Transoxania, and the Tarim Basin'. The shape also runs south to Kabul and Gilgit and takes Dzungaria (56%) and Kara-Khoja (Turfan-Hami 32%): the Duwa page names 'Beshbalik and Dzungaria, Kara-Khoja, Khurasan, Mazandaran, and the Samarkand region' but not Kabul or Gilgit, which stay unverified. Duwa 'invaded Khurasan and Mazandaran' in early 1295 without a lasting gain; 'The northeast part of Duwa's realm was ceded to the Yuan dynasty' after 1306 (undated, not drawn). Cliopatria's relation row makes the khanate a Yuan vassal 1294-1374; the pages date the recognition to 1303 (and 1304 for the general peace).
2.45 M km2, unchanged (-23 cells). 'Tarmashirin (1326–1334) converted to Islam and raided the Delhi Sultanate, reaching as far as Delhi'; Kebek 'reigned until 1325'. No land moved.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, valid for 1344-1345 only (years change; the shape stands)

keyframe_review.note: The page dates the end of the undivided khanate to 1346, six years before Cliopatria's step: 'In 1345 he rebelled against his sovereign, the Chagatai Khan Qazan, but was defeated. The following year he tried again and succeeded in killing the khan.' The Chagatai page: 'split in two during the 1340s'. The shape stands for 1344-1345 only; the new keyframe 1346 holds the eastern part. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1344..1345 from this entry's own 'valid for 1344-1345 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1352 shape, the eastern part (Moghulistan), drawn from 1346; Transoxiana, Fergana and the south go to Qazaghan's amirate

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1346-1359. Qazaghan 'set up Danishmendji as puppet khan' (1346-1348, then Bayan Quli 1348-1358) in the west; 'the Dughlats enthroned a son of Esen Buqa I, Tughlugh Timur as khan of Moghulistan in 1347' (Chagatai page), 'Moghulistan ... became independent in 1347' (Moghulistan page). Cliopatria's 1352 shape (1.66 M km2: Transoxiana, Fergana, Badakhshan and the Afghan south removed) is the eastern part; the western part belongs to the amirate of Qazaghan (no Cliopatria row). Infobox area (3.4 M km2) is the undivided khanate, not comparable.

1.66 M km2 for 1352-1362 (Transoxiana 19%, Fergana 30%, Tarim 66%, Almaliq inside). Right as the eastern khanate: 'governed the Tarim Basin and the steppe area of Moghulistan'; 'The most powerful of the tribes, the Dughlats, controlled extensive territories in Moghulistan and the western Tarim Basin.' Covered by the new keyframe 1346 for 1352-1359 and by the new keyframe 1360 for 1360-1362.

correction.text: the 1352 shape plus Transoxiana, held by Tughlugh Timur and his son Ilyas Khoja

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1360-1362. 'Tughlugh Timur ... invaded in March 1360'; 'In 1360, Tughlugh invaded Transoxania and conquered it' (Chagatai page); 'In 1361, however, Tughlugh Timur and his army rode into the region for the second time' and 'appointed his son Ilyas Khoja as viceroy of Transoxiana'. Cliopatria never draws this: its Chagatai shape holds only 7-19% of Transoxiana from 1352 to 1462.

1.89 M km2, +0.23 M km2 over 1352, all in the Tarim Basin (+787 cells, Tarim 66% to 87%). Tughlugh Timur died in 1363 and 'Amir Husayn and Timur quickly wrested [Transoxiana] from Ilyas Khoja'; the Dughlats 'held several important towns as vassals to the khans, including' Kashgar, Aksu, Yarkand and Khotan (undated). The Tarim step is not explained by a dated sentence (ledger confidence 1).

1.89 M km2, unchanged. 'In 1375, Timur invaded Moghulistan, looting the Ili region.' The Chagatayid heir Khizr Khoja was enthroned by the Dughlats in the 1380s (1389-1390 on his own page). No land moved yet.

1.76 M km2: -401 cells in the west and north (the last of Transoxiana, Tashkent, western Semirechye, the northern steppe). 'Timur sent at least five victorious expeditions to Moghulistan, seriously weakening Qamar-ud-Din's regime' (undated); Khizr Khoja 'took the throne ... after the defeat of' Qamar-ud-din in 1390 and gave his daughter to Timur in 1397. The step is plausibly Timur's but no sentence dates it (ledger confidence 1).
1.76 M km2, -13 cells. Timur 'died at Farab on 17 or 18 February 1405' on the way to China; Khizr Khoja died in 1399. No border moved.
Unchanged (+1 cell). Between Khizr Khoja (d. 1399) and Uwais Khan (1418) the pages give no ruler or event.
Unchanged. Uwais Khan comes to power in 1418 (first reign 1418-1421, again 1425-1429).

1.54 M km2, -743 cells in the north-east: Dzungaria (613 cells), Turfan-Hami (80), Semirechye (76). Uwais Khan 'was twice taken prisoner' by the Oirats and 'frequently defeated by them'; the Oirats 'previously captured Beshbalik and Kumul'; he 'was forced to leave this city under attacks of Oirats' and moved 'to Ilibalik in Ili River Valley', then made Turfan his base. No sentence gives a year, so the Dzungarian loss is bridged on the shape (ledger confidence 1).

Unchanged (+1 cell). Esen Buqa II 'was Khan of Moghulistan from 1429 until his death' (the text says 1428); Kashgar, 'captured by the Timurids after Uwais Khan had died, was retaken in 1435' is not drawn (Cliopatria keeps Kashgar throughout).

Unchanged. 'In 1451 he attacked Tashkent, and a second expedition was undertaken soon afterwards'; he 'besieged and temporarily gained control over Andijan'. No lasting gain, so the shape needs no change.
Unchanged (+3 cells). The Moghul-Timurid frontier on the Syr Darya stays where it was.
Unchanged. 'Esen Buqa died of natural causes in 1462, after a khanship of thirty-three years'; the state ends in 1462 and Cliopatria's Moghulistan row starts in 1463.

region.text: Transoxiana, Semirechye and the Tarim Basin, the Qara Khitai lands Chagatai inherited in 1227

ledger.note: 1294: the Chagatai Khanate stands among the successors of the Mongol Empire, ruled by Duwa. The year is Cliopatria's; the page calls the ulus 'Independent Khanate (1266–1347)' and the Duwa page has Kaidu appoint Duwa 'as head of the Chagatai Khanate' in 1282 (the Chagatai page says after 1274). Confidence 1: bridged on Cliopatria's year.

region.text: Chapar's territory, the Ögedeid ulus of Kaidu (no region named on the page)

ledger.note: 1306: Chapar surrenders to Duwa and the Ögedeid ulus of Kaidu ends. 'After Kaidu's death in 1301, both Duwa and Kaidu's son Chapar recognized Yuan authority in 1303' and Chapar was forced 'to surrender his territory to Duwa in 1306' (Duwa page: after the defeat of Orus in June 1306). The page names no region; Dzungaria, which the 1294 shape already holds, is the researcher's reading. No border moves in the shape.

region.text: the western half: Transoxiana, Fergana, Badakhshan and the south, under Qazaghan and his puppet khans Danishmendji (1346-1348) and Bayan Quli (1348-1358)

ledger.note: 1346: Qazaghan kills Qazan Khan and the khanate splits in two. 'In 1346 a tribal chief, Amir Qazaghan, killed Qazan and set up Danishmendji as puppet khan' (Chagatai page); 'split in two during the 1340s'. Transoxiana, Fergana, Badakhshan and the Afghan south go to the amirs; Cliopatria draws the split only in 1352.

1347: the Dughlats raise Tughlugh Timur and the eastern khanate becomes Moghulistan. 'In 1347 the Dughlats decided to appoint a khan of their own, and raised the Chagatayid Tughlugh Timur to the throne'; 'Moghulistan, which had formed the eastern portion of the Chagatai Khanate, became independent in 1347'. Cliopatria keeps the row (and the colour) as 'Chagatai Khanate' to 1462.

region.text: Transoxiana, in disorder after Qazaghan's murder in 1358

ledger.note: March 1360: Tughlugh Timur invades Transoxiana. 'Tughlugh Timur judged that he would face little resistance in Transoxiana and invaded in March 1360'; 'In 1360 he took advantage of a breakdown of order in Transoxiana' (Moghulistan page).
1361: the second invasion ends the contest. 'In 1361, however, Tughlugh Timur and his army rode into the region for the second time', and he 'appointed his son Ilyas Khoja as viceroy of Transoxiana'.

1361: Transoxiana is Moghul under Ilyas Khoja. 'In 1361, however, Tughlugh Timur and his army rode into the region for the second time'; 'Having destroyed the power of the Transoxianan amirs and reunified the Chagatai Khanate, Tughlugh Timur appointed his son Ilyas Khoja as viceroy of Transoxiana' (Tughlugh Timur page). The Chagatai page puts the conquest in 1360 ('In 1360, Tughlugh invaded Transoxania and conquered it'). Cliopatria never draws it. [Reviewer ia-02-a: source moved to the Tughlugh Timur page, which dates the 1361 conquest.]

region.text: Transoxiana, taken by Amir Husayn and Timur

ledger.note: 1363: Transoxiana is lost. Tughlugh Timur dies in 1363; 'Following Tughlugh's death in 1363, Timur and Amir Husayn took over Transoxiana' (Tughlugh Timur page: 'quickly wrested it from Ilyas Khoja'); the Moghulistan page has Ilyas Khoja rule 1363-1368.

region.text: the western Tarim Basin towns held by the Dughlats: Kashgar, Aksu, Yarkand and Khotan

ledger.note: 1363: the western Tarim joins the shape. Cliopatria adds 787 Tarim cells (Kashgar, Aksu, Yarkand, Khotan side); the page calls those towns Dughlat holdings 'as vassals to the khans' without a year. Confidence 1: bridged on the shape.

1390: Timur beats Qamar-ud-din and Khizr Khoja takes the throne. 'Khizr Khoja took the throne of Moghulistan after the defeat of' Qamar-ud-din; infobox 'Reign: 1390–1399' (succession box 1389; the Moghulistan page says the restoration came 'in the 1380s'). A Chagatayid restoration after the Dughlat regime; the state and colour continue.

region.text: the last of Transoxiana, Tashkent, western Semirechye and the northern steppe edge, lost to Timur's expeditions

ledger.note: 1395: the western and northern fringe goes to Timur. 'Timur sent at least five victorious expeditions to Moghulistan, seriously weakening Qamar-ud-Din's regime' (undated); 'In 1375, Timur invaded Moghulistan, looting the Ili region' (Chagatai page). Confidence 1: bridged on Cliopatria's step of 1395 (-401 cells).

region.text: Dzungaria with Beshbalik and Kumul, and the north-eastern steppe, taken by the Oirats

ledger.note: 1422: Dzungaria goes to the Oirats. Uwais Khan 'was frequently defeated by them ... twice taken prisoner'; the Oirats 'previously captured Beshbalik and Kumul'. No year is given; bridged on Cliopatria's step of 1422 (Dzungaria, 613 cells).

1429: Kashgar passes to the Timurids. 'the town of Kashgar, which had been captured by the Timurids after Uwais Khan had died, was retaken in 1435'; Uwais died in 1428 or 1429 (the pages differ). Not drawn in Cliopatria.
1435: Kashgar is retaken. 'the town of Kashgar, which had been captured by the Timurids after Uwais Khan had died, was retaken in 1435.'

region.text: Tashkent, and Andijan in the Fergana valley

ledger.note: 1451: Esen Buqa II attacks Tashkent. 'In 1451 he attacked Tashkent, and a second expedition was undertaken soon afterwards'; he 'also besieged and temporarily gained control over Andijan' (undated). The Timurids 'had the military strength to defeat the Moghuls in Transoxiana'.
1452: the Moghul attacks on the Syr Darya end without gain. The page gives no end year ('soon afterwards'); the shape of 1453 is unchanged. Confidence 1.

region.text: the whole Moghul khanate, divided between Yunus Khan in the west and Dost Muhammad in the east

ledger.note: 1462: Esen Buqa II dies and Moghulistan divides. 'Esen Buqa died of natural causes in 1462, after a khanship of thirty-three years'; 'in the west Yunus Khan gained power, while in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan'. The Moghulistan page: 'Moghulistan split into two parts: 1462'. Cliopatria's Moghulistan row begins in 1463.

wars.name: Kaidu and Duwa against the Yuan

zones.text: Beshbalik and Uyghuria, where Duwa destroyed 'a force in Uyghuria loyal to Kublai Khan' (1275) and the Yuan were defeated (1276)

wars.outcome: Duwa attacked the Yuan garrisons in the winter of 1298 and was 'wounded and defeated' in 1301; Kaidu died in 1301; Duwa and Chapar recognised Yuan authority in 1303 and a general peace followed 'around 1304'. 'The northeast part of Duwa's realm was ceded to the Yuan dynasty' (undated).
wars.note: Starts before the dossier's first year; the 1294-1303 part is the one that matters to the map. The Chagatai page gives 1275 for Duwa joining Kaidu. [Reviewer ia-02-a: 'from' clipped from 1275 to the dossier's first year, 1294; the war began in 1275 under the Mongol Empire.]

wars.name: Chagatai invasions of the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: Duwa 'invaded Khurasan and Mazandaran' in early 1295 while the Ilkhanid commanders were in a succession struggle; in 1315 Esen Buqa 'invaded the Ilkhanate in support of Duwa's grandson, Dawud Khoja'. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Chagatai raids on the Delhi Sultanate
wars.outcome: Duwa invaded the Punjab in 1297 and was defeated; Prince Turghai looted the Delhi region in 1303; Kebek looted the Multan region in 1305. Tarmashirin (1326-1334) later reached Delhi (undated, tughlaq-dynasty). No land changed hands.

wars.name: Qazaghan's rebellion

zones.text: the western half: Transoxiana, Fergana, Badakhshan and the south

wars.outcome: Qazaghan rebelled in 1345, was defeated, and killed Qazan Khan the next year; the khanate split into a western amirate with puppet khans and the eastern Moghulistan.

wars.name: Tughlugh Timur's conquest of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Tughlugh Timur invaded in March 1360 and again in 1361 and left Ilyas Khoja as viceroy; Amir Husayn and Timur wrested the land back after Tughlugh's death in 1363.
wars.note: The Battle of the Mire (1365) is not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Timur's wars against Moghulistan

zones.text: the western and northern fringe of Moghulistan

wars.outcome: Timur looted the Ili region in 1375, 'sent at least five victorious expeditions to Moghulistan' (undated) and defeated Qamar-ud-din in 1390; Khizr Khoja then ruled as Timur's son-in-law (his daughter married Timur in 1397).
wars.note: Only 1375 and 1390 are dated; the other expeditions are not.

wars.name: Moghul-Oirat wars
wars.outcome: Uwais Khan fought the Oirats 'sixty-one engagements ... only once was he victorious', was twice captured and lost Beshbalik and Kumul; he made Turfan his base and moved to Ilibalik.
wars.note: No year is given for any engagement; the span is the reign of Uwais (1418-1421 and 1425-1429).

wars.name: Moghul-Timurid wars under Esen Buqa II

zones.text: Kashgar, lost after 1428-1429 and retaken in 1435

wars.outcome: The Timurids took Kashgar after Uwais died and Esen Buqa retook it in 1435; in 1451 he attacked Tashkent and temporarily held Andijan. No lasting change.
wars.note: The end year 1452 is the researcher's reading of 'soon afterwards'.

certainty.note: Steppe, oasis and mountain frontiers throughout; no treaty or survey line is on any page opened. The 1304 general peace and the 1397 marriage alliance fix no boundary.

notes: Page budget for 15 shapes: 9 pages, all spent. STRUCTURE: Cliopatria's 'Chagatai Khanate' row (1294-1462) is two states in one: the khanate of Duwa and his heirs to 1346 (Transoxiana plus the Tarim, 2.46 M km2) and, from 1346/1347, the eastern Moghul khanate (1.5-1.9 M km2), which the Chagatai page calls Moghulistan and the Moghulistan page dates 1347-1462. The western half after 1346 (Qazaghan's amirate, then Timur) has no Cliopatria row until the Timurid Empire (1375); it needs a dossier. This dossier keeps one state under the Cliopatria row, with a split (1346) and a rename (1347). The moghulistan row (1463-1518) is another part's. NOT SETTLED: (1) Dates: Duwa enthroned 'after 1274' (Chagatai page) or 1282 (Duwa page; Duwa died 1307 there); Esen Buqa II 1428 (text) or 1429 (infobox); Uwais Khan died 1428 or 1429; Khizr Khoja's restoration 'in the 1380s', 1389 or 1390. (2) The Chagatai page's infobox ends the khanate in 1347, and one sentence runs the line to 1930; the Cliopatria end 1462 is followed. (3) The shape steps of 1363, 1395 and 1422 are bridged at confidence 1 (the pages give no year for the Tarim addition, Timur's expeditions or the Oirat conquest of Dzungaria). (4) The 1294 shape reaches Kabul, Badakhshan (100%) and Gilgit (70%): no page opened supports that south. (5) The Yuan suzerainty: Cliopatria relation 'Allegiance of Chagatai Khanate to Yuan Dynasty' (1294-1374); pages date the recognition to 1303 and the general peace to 1304, and only the yuan-dynasty dossier (ea-06) can record it as a vassal pair. (6) The qocho-kingdom dossier carries a vassal pair to this state for 1335-1370; none of the pages opened here says so, so no matching event is written. (7) The rulers' strip is omitted: the 'List of Chagatai khans' page was not opened and the nine pages give reign years only for some khans. (8) Neighbours with no page-dated border: Kartids and Sarbadars (1344-1351), the Delhi Sultanate (raids only), Golden Horde and White Horde, Ming (Hami and Turfan). Counterparts needing dossiers: amirate-of-qazaghan (western Chagatai ulus under Qazaghan and his puppet khans, 1346-c. 1370), ogedeid-ulus (Kaidu's realm, 1275-1306). Gazetteer: 'Moghulistan' has no region entry (Ili valley, Issyk-Kul, Tarim, Turfan); not used here.
